title: Autosentry: heuristic-driven automatic fallback & circuit safety for 429s, timeouts, and error spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an 'Autosentry' subsystem for Redwood routing that converts service-level signals (429 rate, request timeouts, backend error-rate) into deterministic fallback gestures and circuit-breaker actions. Goals: protect latency/availability SLOs for tiered customers, avoid noisy/thundering fallbacks, allow graceful degradation to lower-cost model variants or regional tiers, and provide observability and operator controls.
background: We currently detect overloads via ad-hoc heuristics in the router which lead to inconsistent fallbacks for critical customers. Recent incidents showed oscillation when a per-tenant spike triggered immediate hard failover to a cheaper model variant, which then caused downstream cold-cache latency spikes when traffic returned. We need a robust, tunable mechanism that fuses multiple signals and enforces hysteresis, safe half-open probing, and per-entity probation windows.
scope:
- Implement signal ingestion (429s, 5xx error counts, p99 request latency, request timeouts) in the router telemetry pipeline.
- Build an Autosentry rules engine that computes a trip score per routing key (region + tier + tenant).
- Circuit states: CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN (degrade with aggressive telemetry), OPEN (fallback active), PROBING (controlled canary to restore).
- Actions: route to lower-tier region, route to cheaper model variant (quantized/compact), or apply client-visible 429 mitigation (rate-limit responses/backpressure).
- Operator UI + Prometheus/Tracing metrics + logs.
- Safe rollout + canary tests and chaos scenarios.
design-decisions: 1) Score-based trip: use weighted fusion of signals (recent 429 ratio, 1m timeout rate, 5m p95 latency increase) instead of single-threshold triggers to reduce flapping. 2) Decaying probation: trip score decays exponentially to allow automatic recovery without full operator intervention. 3) Soft open stage to prefer slower degradations (e.g., model variant with higher latency but lower cost) before hard open. 4) Per-tenant and per-route knobs; defaults conservative for paid tiers. 5) Probing uses tokenized canary requests isolated to avoid cache stampedes.
acceptance_criteria: Autosentry computes trip scores and exposes a metric per (region,tier) and per-tenant key
Circuit transitions follow CLOSED->SOFT_OPEN->OPEN->PROBING->CLOSED with hysteresis and documented time constants
Fallback actions (regional reroute, model-variant switch) can be executed via policy and roll back automatically after successful probing
No increase in mean latency for P0 customers during experiments above 5% versus baseline
Operator Console shows live state, recent triggers, and allows manual override
End-to-end integration test that simulates sustained 429 burst results in stable fallback and recovery without oscillation
implementation_notes:
- Extend router telemetry schema to include per-request outcome tag (success/timeout/429/5xx) and estimate server-side queue length where available.
- New service 'autosentry' written in Go, colocated with router control plane for low-latency decisions.
- Persist state in Redis for quick reads; durable snapshot to Postgres for audits.
- Expose gRPC API for Console and for router to query current circuit state and decision rationale.
- Config: default weights, decay half-life, probe token rate, soft-open percentage; override by customer via policy API.
- Safety: a global kill-switch and per-tenant max-degradation policy to prevent accidental full-fallback for highest-tier customers.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for trip score math (edge cases: division by zero, sparse signals).
2) Integration test harness: synthetic traffic generator that can produce configurable 429/timeouts/errors; verify stable state transitions.
3) Chaos run in staging: inject backend slowdowns and observe Autosentry behavior; measure oscillation count.
4) Load test with 10k tenants to verify state store scales.
5) Quick A/B canary in production on <1% traffic with emergency rollback script.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 1: Deploy autosentry control plane to staging and enable router telemetry ingestion. Run full test suite.
- Stage 2: Canary on a subset of non-enterprise regions for 48h, monitor metrics and rollback on anomalies.
- Stage 3: Enable for P2/P3 customers for 1 week; collect feedback.
- Stage 4: Gradual enablement for P1 customers with conservative defaults and opt-in for P0.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Metrics: trip_score{region,tier,tenant}, circuit_state{region,tier,tenant}, probe_success_rate, fallback_action_count.
Alerts: sustained trip_score>0.8 for 5m, probe_fail_rate>50% for 10m, circuit_state_open count increases by >10% in 15m.
Dashboards: per-region heatmap, per-tenant incident timeline, recent decisions feed.
runbook: If a P0 customer shows unexpected degradation: 1) Check autosentry dashboard for trip_score and recent signals. 2) If in OPEN, trigger manual override to CLOSED for that tenant and collect traces. 3) If oscillating, increase decay half-life and disable probing. 4) Engage on-call runtime team; open incident and link to PR/rollout.

2026-03-13 Design review: add Soft Open to prefer routing to cheaper model variant first before a full regional failover. Also add per-tenant max-degrade policy.
